title: Collections Standard: Repossession Assignment, Recall, Voluntary Surrender and Notices for the Kestrel New Vehicle Retail Installment Sale Contract
content:
**Collections standard, Kestrel New Vehicle Retail Installment Sale Contract.**

1. **Assignment threshold.** An account may be assigned for repossession only when its days past due are at least the tier's minimum days past due for assignment.
2. **Right to cure.** Where the contract records a right-to-cure period greater than 0 days, assignment may occur only after a right-to-cure notice has been mailed and that many calendar days have run from the right-to-cure notice date recorded on the contract.
3. **Recall.** While the account is repossession assigned, the assignment is recalled when the customer pays all past-due installments and all late charges due in certified funds before the vehicle is recovered; a partial payment or a promise to pay does not recall it.
4. **Voluntary surrender.** A customer may voluntarily surrender the vehicle at any time while the contract is active; the surrender is the customer's own act, scheduled at a location the company designates, and the voluntary agency fee applies instead of the involuntary fee.
5. **Notices.** A notice can be mailed only while the contract status is active, repossession assigned, repossessed, deficiency or paid in full. The notice of intent to sell is mailed within the product's notice period in business days after the repossession date and states the scheduled sale date and the redemption and any reinstatement amount. A deficiency notice is mailed after a sale that leaves a balance and a surplus notice after a sale that leaves a surplus; mailing dates are recorded on the contract.
6. **Bankruptcy.** When the customer reports an active bankruptcy filing, or the bankruptcy status on the customer profile is anything other than none, no collection or repossession step is taken by the servicing desk.

## Recall test

| Paid before recovery, in certified funds | Assignment recalled |
|---|---|
| All past-due installments and all late charges due | Yes |
| Part of them | No |
| A promise to pay | No |

*Hypothetical:* a Tier 1 account at 89 days past due has not reached the 90-day assignment minimum of its tier; at 90 days it has, and where its contract records a right-to-cure period, a notice must also have been mailed and that period must have run.
